newsitem.title: UK: US Maritime Administration OKs new Lykes subsidy.
newsitem.headline: US Maritime Administration OKs new Lykes subsidy.

text.p: Lykes Bros Steamship Co said the US Maritime Administration (Marad) has approved a $2 million subsidy payment which will help secure its liquidity while discussions about its takeover by Canadian Pacific Ltd continue.
The Florida-based container shipping company said Marad has completed an audit concerning its operational differential subsidy contract covering the past five years.
"This audit will result in additional subsidy payments to Lykes in excess of $2 million which Lykes expects to receive as soon as certain details are resolved."
Chairman and chief executive officer of Lykes, Joe Freeman said: "Receipt of these funds will go a long way to stabilising the cash situation."
Lykes is currently under Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection while it seeks approval from Marad for a $30 million take-over by CP Ships, a unit of Canadian Pacific.

The take-over has hit opposition from rival US shipping groups and seafarers unions over the issue of operational subsidies for US-flagged ships which are kept available for military use following the company's take-over by a foreign group.
Freeman said that US citizenship and ownership issues raised at Marad would be addressed by the reorganised Lykes being owned in the US.

"It will be owned by GATX Corp and Gilman Financial Corporation, substantial bona fide US citizens, and will be independent of foreigners." Canadian Pacific will acquire certain of Lykes' assets, he added.
Subsidy payments would be made to the new company, named Sea Crews ll.
"The final proposal will meet the applicable requirements and will merit approval," he added.

Freeman said: "The additional operating differential subsidy funds, the key creditor discussions, and the progress on discussions with the Marad staff make me very confident that liquidity issues will not be a factor while the orderly process of obtaining approval for the transaction proceeds."
Lykes said it had received support from 200 of its shippers, several creditors and its unions for approval of the take-over plan.
